Questionnaire workflows

Source: vignettes/questionnaire.Rmd
questionnaire.Rmd

shad_questionnaire() is an experimental, bookmarkable Shiny input for a sequence of single-choice, multiple-choice, and freeform questions. Define the questions as data with shad_question(). The browser owns navigation and answer state; the server receives one stable value and can patch it with update_shad_questionnaire().

Define questions

Choice question vectors use names as stable values and their contents as the labels. Unnamed vectors use the same string for both value and label. Explicit value/label lists are useful when labels need to be distinct from stable values.

library(shiny)
library(shadshiny)

questions <- list(
  shad_question(
    "direction", "What should be built?",
    description = "Choose the first milestone.",
    choices = c(data = "Server table", rtl = "RTL"),
    shortcuts = c(data = "1", rtl = "2")
  ),
  shad_question(
    "features", "Which features are needed?",
    type = "multiple",
    choices = list(
      list(value = "search", label = "Search"),
      list(value = "export", label = "Export")
    )
  ),
  shad_question(
    "notes", "Anything else?", type = "text",
    required = FALSE, skippable = TRUE
  ),
  shad_question(
    "details", "What belongs in the server table?", type = "text",
    required = TRUE, show_if = list(direction = "data")
  )
)

show_if is deliberately limited to named equality data. Every listed condition must match for the question to be visible. It is serialized into the markup and evaluated as a comparison in the browser; it never evaluates R or JavaScript supplied by an application or a user.

Compose the input

All question fieldsets are rendered once. The active question is visible; inactive and conditionally hidden questions have both hidden and inert, so their answers and DOM identity remain stable without leaving hidden controls in the keyboard order.

questionnaire <- do.call(
  shad_questionnaire,
  c(
    list(
      inputId = "onboarding",
      progress_label = "Step %s of %s",
      previous_label = "Back",
      next_label = "Continue",
      skip_label = "Not now",
      submit_label = "Finish"
    ),
    questions
  )
)

ui <- page_shad(questionnaire, verbatimTextOutput("state"))

The result is a regular Shiny input. Native fieldset/legend, radio, checkbox, and text controls provide the semantic form structure, while the progressbar, live status region, error slots, and real buttons provide the navigation feedback.

Read the value

input$onboarding always has this shape:

Field Type Meaning
active integer Current question, 1-based and including hidden definitions.
answers named list Answers keyed by stable question name. Multiple answers are character vectors.
skipped character vector Question names explicitly skipped by the user.
complete logical TRUE after all visible required questions pass and the user submits or completes an optional flow. 
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$state <- renderPrint(input$onboarding)

  observeEvent(input$onboarding$complete, {
    req(isTRUE(input$onboarding$complete))
    message("Answers received: ", paste(names(input$onboarding$answers), collapse = ", "))
  }, ignoreInit = TRUE)
}

Hidden branch answers stay in answers when a prior response makes their question unavailable. Hidden questions do not contribute to progress or validation. This lets an application preserve a user’s work while they explore another branch, and the application can decide whether to discard it on submit.

Validation and server updates

Required questions block Next and focus their first native control. Optional questions can be skipped explicitly when skippable = TRUE. Server-side rules can return named errors without replacing the user’s answers:

observeEvent(input$validate, {
  errors <- list()
  details <- input$onboarding$answers$details
  if (identical(input$onboarding$answers$direction, "data") &&
      (is.null(details) || !nzchar(details))) {
    errors$details <- "Describe the table before finishing."
  }
  update_shad_questionnaire("onboarding", errors = errors, session = session)
})

observeEvent(input$load_draft, {
  update_shad_questionnaire(
    "onboarding",
    active = 2L,
    answers = list(direction = "data", features = c("search")),
    session = session
  )
})

observeEvent(input$start_over, {
  update_shad_questionnaire("onboarding", reset = TRUE, session = session)
})

active is a 1-based question index. answers and errors must be named lists so their keys remain stable in modules. Updates are partial: omitted facets are left alone. reset = TRUE clears active state, answers, skipped questions, errors, and completion.

Bookmarking

The constructor passes its initial value through shiny::restoreInput(), so the complete state can be restored by Shiny bookmarking:

enableBookmarking("url")

ui <- page_shad(
  shad_questionnaire(
    "survey",
    shad_question("plan", "Choose a plan", choices = c(free = "Free", pro = "Pro")),
    shad_question("notes", "Notes", type = "text", required = FALSE),
    value = list(
      active = 2L,
      answers = list(plan = "pro", notes = "Keep this draft"),
      skipped = character(),
      complete = FALSE
    )
  )
)

Use the same constructor for enableBookmarking("server"); persistence remains Shiny’s responsibility. The questionnaire does not write to URLs, databases, or browser storage itself.

Modules

The generic Shiny binding and updater resolve namespaced ids through the active reactive domain. Keep the question names stable within each instance and use the ordinary module pattern:

survey_ui <- function(id) {
  ns <- NS(id)
  do.call(shad_questionnaire, c(
    list(inputId = ns("survey")),
    list(
      shad_question("plan", "Choose a plan", choices = c(free = "Free", pro = "Pro")),
      shad_question("notes", "Notes", type = "text", required = FALSE)
    )
  ))
}

survey_server <- function(id) {
  moduleServer(id, function(input, output, session) {
    observeEvent(input$load, {
      update_shad_questionnaire(
        "survey", answers = list(plan = "pro"), session = session
      )
    })
  })
}

The questionnaire is framework-free at runtime. Conditions, answers, labels, and errors are inserted as text or JSON data; no user-supplied string is compiled as code or inserted as raw HTML.
